questions.stem: What can you conclude about the system y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x - 5?
questions.subject: INTEGRATED_1

answer.exemplar: The solution of a system is the point where the two graphs cross, because a shared point has to satisfy both equations. Parallel lines never cross, so graphs of y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x - 5 can have no shared point, and the system has no solution. Algebraically, setting the two expressions equal reduces the system to the statement 1 = -5, which is false, so there is no value of x that can work. Two distinct parallel lines therefore correspond exactly to a system with no solution, whereas coincident lines would give infinitely many solutions.

questions.explanation: The geometric and algebraic descriptions of a system are two views of one fact, so an impossible system and non-intersecting graphs must correspond. Setting the two expressions for y equal asks for an x that would make them identical, and when the slopes match, the x cancels and only a false constant statement is left. That false statement is the algebraic signature of parallel lines that never meet.
questions.hint: Relate the crossing of the two graphs to the single shared point of the system.
questions.learningObjective: explain graphically why a system can have no solution
